2608.05015.title: Revealed Rationality: Label-Free Evaluation and Regularization from Representation Theorems
2608.05015.paper_summary: Representation theorems in decision theory establish that behavior satisfies certain axioms if and only if it can be rationalized by a well-defined objective. I argue that this ``if and only if'' structure provides a potentially useful foundation for label-free evaluation and regularization of LLMs and other AI systems. Axiom compliance can be checked from the model's own responses to synthetic choice problems, with no external labels or human feedback, and the penalties are readily computable. Because the axioms are necessary and sufficient, the resulting checks exhaust the implications of the relevant rationality standard for the elicited data: a model that passes cannot be rejected on rationality grounds by any further test of the same data. I discuss three instantiations: probabilistic coherence via a theorem of de Finetti, preference rationality via Afriat's theorem, and subjective expected utility via a theorem of Echenique and Saito (2015), each yielding a continuous penalty that is zero whenever behavior can be rationalized. Since coherence does not restrict which objective rationalizes behavior, these penalties complement rather than replace other evaluation and training signals.
2608.05015.paper_summary_zh: 決策理論中的表徵定理確立了行為滿足某些公理的條件，當且僅當它可以被明確定義的目標所合理化。我主張這種「當且僅當」的結構為無標籤的評估和 LLM 及其他 AI 系統的正則化提供了一個潛在有用的基礎。公理的遵循可以從模型對合成選擇問題的自身反應中檢查，無需外部標籤或人類反饋，且罰金是可以輕易計算的。由於這些公理是必要且充分的，因此所得到的檢查耗盡了相關理性標準對所引出數據的含義：一個通過檢查的模型不會因為同一數據的任何進一步測試而在理性基礎上被拒絕。我討論了三個具體實例：通過 de Finetti 的定理實現的概率一致性、通過 Afriat 的定理實現的偏好理性，以及通過 Echenique 和 Saito（2015）的定理實現的主觀期望效用，每一種都產生一個連續的罰金，當行為可以被合理化時，該罰金為零。由於一致性不限制哪個目標合理化行為，因此這些罰金是對其他評估和訓練信號的補充，而不是替代。
2608.05015.author: Isaiah Andrews et.al.
